title: MAXIM: Multi-Axis MLP for Image Processing
grouping: The two branches sit in large rounded tinted bands, the upper pale pink and the lower pale green, named in bold coloured words to their left ('Local Branch' in red, 'Global Branch' in green). A vertical dashed rule separates the main block from a right-hand detail panel titled 'gMLP Block' in bold blue on a pale-blue rounded background, inside which a grey rounded inner container holds the gating unit.
shapes_depth: Feature tensors are flat 2-D grids of square cells (6 x 4) that show the token layout; blocking and gridding are drawn as the grid split into separate small grids, and the processed grids outline their cells in different colours (red, green, blue, magenta, orange) to show which tokens are mixed together. Layers (LayerNorm, Dense, GELU) are tall narrow rounded boxes with rotated labels and pastel fills; in the detail panel the same layers are horizontal pills stacked bottom to top. Tensor shapes in bracket notation ([6, 4, C/2], [3 x 2, 2 x 2, C/2]) above or below each grid, with the numbers that change coloured red (local) or green (global). Shortcuts are dashed arrows.
proposed_highlight: 'gMLP' is bold blue wherever it is applied, matching the detail panel's title; branch colours tie each band's title, its shape numbers and its operation labels together.
lesson: Draw the token layout as an actual small grid of cells at each reshaping step (split, blocked, processed, unblocked) and colour the shape numbers that change in the branch's own colour, so the reshaping reads from the drawing alone.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: multi-axis gated MLP block for image restoration

core.what: two equally wide tinted lanes, pink Local Branch above and green Global Branch below, run the same four-step tensor sequence (split, block/grid, gMLP, unblock/ungrid) in parallel between one shared stem and one concat tail

relations.form: the pink and green bands are stacked with identical columns (1/2 Heads grid, blocked/gridded input, processed, 1/2 Heads grid), so the Block-vs-Grid difference reads by comparing the two rows column by column
left to right: LayerNorm-Dense-GELU stem, Split Heads into the two bands, Concat Heads, Dense, then an add node; a dashed shortcut rises at the left and re-enters at the add

each operation is drawn on a literal 6 x 4 token grid: blocking cuts it into 2 x 2 windows, gridding interleaves it, and the processed grids outline the mixed tokens in red/green/blue/magenta/orange to show which cells one gMLP mixes

a separate pale-blue 'gMLP Block' panel behind a dashed vertical rule at the far right opens the gMLP step bottom to top (LayerNorm, Dense, GELU, Split, LayerNorm, Spatial Proj, multiply, Dense, add), tied to the bands only by the blue 'gMLP' word

channels.colour: band tint and title colour = branch (pink/red local, green global), and the same red/green colours the changing numbers in shape annotations; box fill = layer type (grey norm, green Dense, purple GELU, pink Spatial Proj, yellow Split); outline colour on processed grids = token group mixed together - so red and green carry both branch identity and, in the processed grids, mixing groups
channels.shape: cell grids = tensors; rounded upright rectangles = layers; circles = add / multiply
channels.line: solid arrows = data flow; dashed arrows = shortcut connections
channels.frame: tinted rounded band = one branch; pale-blue panel behind a dashed rule = the opened gMLP block

quality.strengths: the local/global contrast is geometry: two identical lanes whose only drawn difference is how the 6 x 4 grid is cut (contiguous 2 x 2 windows vs interleaved grid), with the mixed tokens outlined so the reader sees which cells meet; tensor shapes in brackets colour only the dimension that changes; the gMLP internals are taught once in a side panel instead of repeated
quality.weaknesses: red and green mean branch in the titles and shape numbers but token-group in the processed grid outlines, which also use blue, magenta and orange; the detail panel is linked to the bands only by the word 'gMLP', not by a callout or matching tint

insights.structure: A main block with two stacked rounded tinted bands (pale pink 'Local Branch', pale green 'Global Branch', titles in bold red/green to their left) between a shared LayerNorm-Dense-GELU stem and a Concat-Dense-add tail, plus a separate pale-blue 'gMLP Block' detail panel at the far right behind a dashed rule.
insights.data: Tensors are drawn as literal 6 x 4 cell grids at each step (split, blocked/gridded, processed, unblocked), with processed cells outlined in different colours to show which tokens are mixed, and bracket shape annotations like [3 x 2, 2 x 2, C/2] whose changing numbers are coloured red or green.
insights.emphasis: The word 'gMLP' is bold blue at each application in both branches and matches the detail panel's blue title, while each branch's colour ties its title, its shape numbers and its axis label together.
insights.flow: Left to right through the stem, splitting into the two bands that run in parallel to a concat, then a dashed shortcut arrow from the stem rejoins at the final add; the detail panel reads bottom to top with a skip arrow up its left side.
insights.avoid: The multi-coloured cell outlines in the processed grids carry a lot of meaning but are too thin to decode at print size, and the gridded global result is hard to tell apart from the blocked local one.

arrangement.units: two horizontal tinted bands, one per branch, each running from its split grid to its merged grid; a separate framed detail panel at the right
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare arrow into the LayerNorm stem; data as cell grids inside each band
arrangement.shared: stem and tail layers drawn once outside the bands
